title: the ring-26 silence decomposed (3 root causes, none is earlyprintk), and the study's own EFI stub boots the chain end to end
inherits: vol5-os-boot/1.0 (same kernel, same FAT16 superfloppy, same FW26 markers)

kernel.fat_copy_note: read back from the superfloppy via mtools — byte-identical, the FAT content is acquitted

ring26_open_thread.registered: the hand-built UKI loads and STARTS under OVMF (BdsDxe "starting", no failure status) but stays silent — earlyprintk debugging deferred to the next session
ring26_open_thread.resolution: the silence is TWO stacked causes and a dead-end hypothesis, all measured in ring 27; earlyprintk was never reachable — the stub died before any kernel printk, and its own ConOut errors were invisible under the ring-26 NVRAM

root_causes.name: the UKI shape is inert on the x86 stub — .cmdline/.initrd sections are NEVER read
root_causes.evidence: v6.12 x86-stub.c: cmdline = efi_convert_cmdline(LoadOptions); initrd = LoadFile2 device path or cmdline initrd=; the PE sections belong to systemd-stub, which is not in the image. Arm A/C: pristine kernel speaks+panics WITH the 1 MiB initramfs still embedded in its own PE (arm A) — the stub never consumed it.
root_causes.consequence: a "UKI" without systemd-stub is a kernel with dead weight; the ring-26 objcopy recipe was mechanically perfect and architecturally moot

root_causes.name: the decompression-buffer knife-edge: efi_random_alloc for max(output_len, kernel_total_size) fails near 512 MiB on the disk path
root_causes.evidence: v6.12 x86-stub.c efi_decompress_kernel: alloc_size = ALIGN(max(output_len, kernel_total_size), MIN_KERNEL_ALIGN) via efi_random_alloc(EFI_LOADER_CODE, LOAD_PHYSICAL_ADDR, ULONG_MAX); failure keeps the EFI_OUT_OF_RESOURCES status and prints the MISLEADING "Failed to decompress kernel" (x86-stub.c:1000) — no decompressor ever ran. fw_cfg floor measured: 128 MiB FAIL / 192 MiB OK → alloc_size ∈ (~55, ~120] MiB. Disk path at 512 MiB: 5/5 stub-fails WITH the UKI pre-loaded (13.2 MiB LoaderCode), then C speaks with the pristine exec — the margin is single-digit MiB at that size.
root_causes.consequence: ring-26's "Out of Resources" lesson (~49 MiB on a 128 MiB VM) and this are one class at two scales; the vendor firmware reports OOR and stays mute about the mechanism

root_causes.name: empty LoadOptions = a silent kernel even when the boot succeeds
root_causes.evidence: the UKI auto-boot at 512/1024 MiB sometimes SUCCEEDS the allocation and then hangs the VM silently: kernel runs with no console=, panics or waits invisibly (no -no-reboot escape from a mute panic)
root_causes.consequence: the earlyprintk front is closed with its true answer: earlyprintk was never the bottleneck — delivering the cmdline is

root_causes.name: LoadOptions are CHAR16-only for the x86 stub (v1 stub lesson, caught before publication)
root_causes.evidence: v6.12 efi_convert_cmdline: options_chars = options_size / sizeof(efi_char16_t); a CHAR8 buffer becomes UTF-16 mojibake (first CHAR16 0x6f63 → 3-byte garbage) → no console= → silent boot. FW27 v1 boot: full trail green up to "Loaded initrd", then silence. Fix: OUR stub widens its CHAR8 .cmdline section to CHAR16 — what systemd-stub does.
root_causes.consequence: the UEFI Shell works because IT passes CHAR16; the EFI_LOAD_OPTION descriptor path has its own FW_BUG quirk in the kernel

root_causes.name: the 6.12 LoadFile2 size-probe contract: EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL, not EFI_SUCCESS
root_causes.evidence: v6.12 efi_load_initrd_dev_path: "status = lf2->load_file(lf2, dp, false, &initrd->size, NULL); if (status != EFI_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL) return EFI_LOAD_ERROR" — a spec-naive provider breaks the load; FW27 implements the exact contract and the kernel line "Loaded initrd from LINUX_EFI_INITRD_MEDIA_GUID device path" confirms consumption
root_causes.consequence: registered as a spec-vs-consumer divergence (UEFI spec: Buffer=NULL → EFI_SUCCESS with the size)

fwcfg_ram_floor.bound: alloc_size ∈ (~55, ~120] MiB; the Debian System.map is a -dbg pointer stub, so this is the only measurement available

disk_probe_matrix.C_pristine_control_512: SPEAKS then panics exactly as predicted (VFS: Unable to mount root fs) — no UKI pre-load, the 13.2 MiB LoaderCode block was the straw

debugcon 0x402 on Debian OVMF plain: mute (RELEASE build) — the vendor voice does not exist, we built our own

fw27_stub.architecture: OVMF auto-boots \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI = FW27-stub: (1) speaks on ConOut; (2) dumps a memory-map summary — the observability the vendor refuses; (3) walks ITS OWN PE section table and consumes .cmdline/.initrd — the ring-26 sections finally read, by OUR code; (4) installs EFI_LOAD_FILE2 on LINUX_EFI_INITRD_MEDIA_GUID (RC5 contract); (5) LoadImage \boot\vmlinuz from the same FAT via a device path built from the volume\'s, sets LoadOptions (CHAR16-widened .cmdline, RC4), StartImage; (6) if the kernel returns, prints the status — the vendor never tells you why
fw27_stub.build: gnu-efi 3.0.18-1+deb13u1 (trixie, extracted root-less per the house playbook) + gcc 14.2.0 + ld -T elf_x86_64_efi.lds + objcopy --target=efi-app-x86-64; .cmdline (81 B) + .initrd (1,063,434 B) appended post-build with the ring-26 VMAs recipe
fw27_stub.size_of_image: 0x115000 (~1.1 MiB — vs the 13.2 MiB UKI: the knife-edge load disappears)
fw27_stub.gnu_efi_note: 3.0.18 headers lack EFI_LOAD_FILE2_PROTOCOL (UEFI 2.2+) — defined in our source from UEFI 2.10 §13.6

fw27_chain.path: OVMF plain 4M -> FatDxe -> \EFI\BOOT\BOOTX64.EFI (FW27-stub) -> LoadImage(\boot\vmlinuz) -> kernel EFI stub <- initrd via OUR LoadFile2 + cmdline via OUR section (widened to CHAR16) -> busybox /init

FW27-stub v1: the study's own loader speaks
FW27 memmap: 112 descriptors, conventional 462 MiB in 9 regions
FW27 sections: .cmdline 81 B, .initrd 1063434 B — consumed by OUR code
FW27: pristine kernel loaded from the same volume
FW27: LoadOptions set (164 B CHAR16 from the .cmdline section), starting the kernel
EFI stub: Loaded initrd from LINUX_EFI_INITRD_MEDIA_GUID device path
fw27_chain.initrd_consumption_proof: the kernel's own line names the LINUX_EFI_INITRD_MEDIA_GUID device path — the fw_cfg path is absent in this boot, so OUR protocol instance is the only source

honesty: the disk was modified in ring 27 (BOOTX64.EFI = FW27 stub; the ring-26 UKI preserved as BOOTX64.NOB; NvVars churn) — the ring-26 artifact's disk sha256 describes the disk BEFORE these changes; every transformation is a persisted mtools command in the session scripts
the coreboot world is UNCHANGED: same ring-24 specimen, same syslinux chain; ring 27 adds no coreboot claim
TCG absolute times are not hardware times; ring 27 adds no timing claim at all
the fw_cfg floor (128/192 MiB) is a single-run ladder, not a median — the bound is honest, not tight
the disk-path knife-edge at 512 MiB is non-deterministic (allocation headroom vs OVMF's own churn + KASLR seed); the matrix records both outcomes
FW27 v1 had the CHAR16 mojibake bug (RC4) — kept in the source comments and the trail (the first W run) as registered history, per house rules
